newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 31.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
- Retail sales in the Northeast appear to have lagged behind those in the rest of the country in 1996.
- Money trickled into equity mutual funds in December at the slowest pace since July.
- Sales of existing homes rebounded in November after five straight months of decline.

- While commercial insurers still cover the most disastrous incidents, more and more companies are insuring themselves against smaller claims and banding together to pool risk against mid-sized claims.
- Aegon of the Netherlands said it was buying the insurance business of Providian for $2.62 billion in stock.
- Tandy said it would close its Incredible Universe stores.
- AT&T is spinning off NCR for less than half the $7.48 billion it paid for the computer maker in 1991.
- Humana said it would cut 700 to 900 jobs next year.
- Banc One said it agreed to buy Liberty Bancorporation for $546 million in stock.

- After less than a year as president and publisher of the HarperCollins trade publishing group, Jack McKeown has resigned. - China's robust economy has expanded at the slowest rate in five years during 1996.
- Executives at Citic Pacific, China's largest investment vehicle in Hong Kong, acquired 15.5 percent of the company from its state-owned parent, Citic Hong Kong.
